objects.description: Result container for an asynchronous QProcess execution. Holds exit code, exit status (mapped to FailedToStart/NormalExit/Crashed), and captured stdout/stderr. Provides convenience predicates success(), crashed(), and failedToStart(). Intended to be delivered to user callbacks from the run(...) helpers.

Lightweight wrapper around QNetworkReply providing convenience methods for finished/success/timeout status, data retrieval, error info, and retry suggestion. It holds a reference to a live QNetworkReply and tracks finished/timeout flags.
Event object passed to progress callbacks; extends NetworkReply with received and total byte counts. Represents interim or final progress state.
Event object passed to completion callbacks; extends NetworkReply and always marks finished=true, with a timeout flag indicating if the operation timed out.

High-level wrapper around QNetworkAccessManager that provides timed GET/POST/HEAD requests with callback-based completion (reply) and progress notifications. Manages timeouts via QTimer and ensures single completion via synchronization. Thread-safety provided for completion gating using QMutex.

Qt-based helper class that queues execution of a stored std::function on the event loop. On construction, connects a run signal to a private slot (meaw) with QueuedConnection and immediately emits run to invoke the function asynchronously.

Interface-like example class documenting the expected minimal API for an application type usable with the helpers in this header. It provides a constructor taking args{QApplication&}, a start(QByteArray) to initialize the first instance, and hasEvent(QByteArray) to handle messages from subsequent instances.
Argument carrier for AppTypeInterface constructor, containing a reference to an existing QApplication.

functions.name: utils::misc::unique_rsc
functions.signature:
template <typename Function, typename Deleter, typename... Arguments>
auto utils::misc::unique_rsc(Function&& function, Deleter&& deleter, Arguments&&... args)
functions.description: Constructs and returns a std::unique_ptr that owns a resource created by function(args...) and destroyed by deleter. The resource-creating function must return a pointer type; the deleter is stored in the unique_ptr (type-decayed). Typical use: wrapping C APIs like fopen/fclose.
requirements: function must be callable with the provided Arguments... and return a pointer type P* (may be nullptr).
The pointee type A = std::remove_pointer_t<std::result_of_t<Function(Arguments&&...)>> must be well-formed.
deleter must be callable as deleter(A*) and be storable inside std::unique_ptr<A, std::decay_t<Deleter>> (i.e., CopyConstructible/MoveConstructible as required by decay).
Arguments... are perfectly-forwarded; ensure they are valid for the call and beware of moved-from states when passing rvalues.
Ownership semantics: the returned unique_ptr exclusively owns the resource and will invoke deleter on reset/destruction; do not free the resource manually.
Exception behavior of function or deleter is unspecified; callers must handle exceptions thrown during construction if function throws.
This utility requires headers <memory> and type traits used by the implementation to be available; C++ standard compatibility of std::result_of may vary (deprecated in C++17).

functions.name: utils::misc::unique_ptr::operator*
functions.description: Dereferences this smart pointer wrapper and returns a reference to the managed object by forwarding to the underlying handle’s operator*(). This is a thin wrapper around std::unique_ptr or std::shared_ptr depending on Qt version.
requirements: The underlying pointer must not be null; dereferencing a null handle results in undefined behavior.
The contained object must be valid for reference access.
Thread-safety follows that of the underlying smart pointer; unspecified here.

functions.name: utils::misc::unique_ptr::operator->
functions.description: Provides pointer-like access to the managed object by forwarding to the underlying handle’s operator->(). Wrapper around std::unique_ptr or std::shared_ptr depending on Qt version.
requirements: The underlying pointer must not be null; calling operator-> on a null handle results in undefined behavior.
The returned pointer is only valid as long as this wrapper (and underlying handle) outlives the use.

functions.name: utils::misc::unique_ptr::get
functions.description: Returns the raw pointer managed by this wrapper by forwarding to the underlying handle’s get(). Does not transfer ownership.
requirements: The returned pointer may be nullptr; callers must check before use.
The pointer remains valid only while the wrapper (and any shared ownership) keeps the object alive; do not delete it manually.

functions.name: utils::qtimer::run
functions.signature:
template< typename Function, typename std::enable_if< std::is_same< utils::qtimer::details::result_of< Function, int >, bool >::value, int >::type = 0 >
void utils::qtimer::run(int interval, Function&& function)
functions.description: Schedules a recurring QTimer that invokes the provided callable with an incrementing counter on each timeout and stops when the callable returns true. Intended for periodic polling or retry loops driven by Qt's event loop. The callback is invoked with the number of elapsed timeouts (starting from 1) and must return true to stop the timer; returning false keeps it running. Internally creates a QTimer with start(interval) and deletes itself and the timer when stopping. Interval is Qt QTimer's interval (milliseconds, inferred from Qt). Requires a running Qt event loop in the calling thread (inferred from QTimer usage).
requirements: Function must be invocable as bool(int) — it takes a single int argument (the call count) and returns a bool indicating whether to stop.
Function must be storable by value and movable/copyable into the internal Timer (it is captured and stored).
The function may be called multiple times until it returns true.
Must be called from a thread with a running Qt event loop so QTimer::timeout and deleteLater can be processed (inferred from QTimer semantics).
The interval argument is intended to be a non-negative duration in milliseconds as per QTimer::start (inferred from Qt; exact constraints not stated in the header).
There is no external handle to cancel; stopping is controlled solely by the callback returning true (behavior inferred from implementation).

Exceptions thrown by the callback will propagate through the Qt signal/slot invocation and may cause undefined behavior; users should avoid throwing across the boundary (inferred best practice; not explicitly stated).

functions.name: utils::qprocess::run
functions.signature:
template <typename Events>
void utils::qprocess::run(const QString& cmd, const QStringList& args, Events events)
functions.description: Asynchronously launches an external process (cmd with args) using QProcess and dispatches lifecycle events to a user-supplied Events handler. The Events type must define hooks for creation, start, stdout/stderr data, errors, and completion. The function returns immediately; the internally created QObject self-deletes after completion or a failed start. Use this when you need fine-grained, streaming access to process I/O and state via custom callbacks.
requirements: Must be called from a thread with a running Qt event loop; signals are connected with Qt::QueuedConnection and the helper QObject uses deleteLater().
cmd must refer to an executable discoverable by QProcess (path or in PATH).

Events type must provide the following callable members with these exact parameter types:
- void whenCreated(QProcess&)
- void whenStarted(QProcess&)
- void withData(QProcess::ProcessChannel, const QByteArray&)
- void withError(QProcess::ProcessError)
- void whenDone(int, QProcess::ExitStatus)
Process output is delivered incrementally via withData; the handler is responsible for buffering if needed.
On QProcess::ProcessError::FailedToStart, withError is invoked and the helper object schedules self-deletion; no further events are guaranteed.
This API is fully asynchronous; do not assume the process has started or finished when run() returns.
Thread-affinity: all callbacks occur in the thread whose event loop owns the created helper QObject (the calling thread at invocation time).

functions.name: utils::qthread::run
functions.signature:
template<typename T, typename std::enable_if<!std::is_void<decltype(std::declval<T>().bg())>::value, int>::type = 0>
void utils::qthread::run(T bgt)
functions.description: Starts a background task on a QThread and, when it finishes, posts the result back to the caller thread. The type T must expose methods: R bg() running in a worker thread and void fg(R) running in the caller thread. Intended for offloading work to a background thread and then delivering the result to the UI/main thread.
requirements: T must be MoveConstructible (it is moved into the thread object).
T must provide a callable method R bg() where R = decltype(std::declval<T>().bg()).
T must provide a callable method void fg(R) to consume the result on the caller thread.
bg() must be thread-safe and must not assume caller-thread affinity.
The object state captured inside T must remain valid until fg() has been invoked (lifetime must outlive the async operation).
Qt must be initialized sufficiently for QThread signal/slot delivery (a Q(Core)Application should exist).
Exceptions or errors thrown from bg() or fg() are not handled by the utility (behavior on exception is unspecified).

functions.name: utils::qthread::await
functions.signature:
template<typename BackGroundTask, typename std::enable_if<!std::is_void<utils::qthread::details::result_of<BackGroundTask>>::value, int>::type = 0>
utils::qthread::details::result_of<BackGroundTask> utils::qthread::await(BackGroundTask bgt)
functions.description: Runs a background callable on a QThread and blocks the caller using a local QEventLoop until completion, then returns the callable's non-void result. Useful for synchronously waiting for an asynchronous operation's result without blocking the worker thread.
requirements: BackGroundTask must be MoveConstructible and invocable with signature R() where R = utils::qthread::details::result_of<BackGroundTask>.
BackGroundTask must be thread-safe and must not interact with UI-thread-only objects.
A Q(Core)Application must exist so that a QEventLoop can run; otherwise event delivery/threads will not function.
Caller must be prepared for re-entrancy while the local QEventLoop runs (events for the caller thread may be processed).
Exceptions thrown by the callable are not handled by the utility (unspecified behavior).

functions.name: utils::network::details::NetworkReply::finished
functions.description: Returns true if the associated network operation has been marked finished in this wrapper. Intended for use inside callbacks to check whether the reply has completed.
requirements: May be called only while the underlying QNetworkReply is valid.
No side effects; safe to call multiple times.

functions.name: utils::network::details::NetworkReply::success
functions.description: Returns true if the underlying QNetworkReply reports no error and the operation did not time out. Useful to gate processing of reply data.
requirements: Underlying QNetworkReply must still be valid when calling.
Time-out state is tracked by the wrapper; success() will be false if a time-out occurred.

functions.name: utils::network::details::NetworkReply::timeOut
functions.description: Returns true if the operation timed out according to the manager’s timer logic.
requirements: Underlying QNetworkReply must still be valid when calling.

functions.name: utils::network::details::NetworkReply::data
functions.description: Reads and returns all available data from the underlying QNetworkReply using readAll(). Typical use is after success() is true.
requirements: Call only while the underlying QNetworkReply is valid.
readAll() drains the reply buffer; subsequent calls may return empty unless more data arrives.

functions.name: utils::network::details::NetworkReply::error
functions.description: Returns the QNetworkReply::NetworkError code from the underlying reply.
requirements: Underlying QNetworkReply must still be valid when calling.

functions.name: utils::network::details::NetworkReply::errorString
functions.description: Returns the human-readable error string from the underlying QNetworkReply.
requirements: Underlying QNetworkReply must still be valid when calling.

functions.name: utils::network::details::NetworkReply::networkReply
functions.description: Returns a reference to the underlying QNetworkReply. Enables direct access to Qt APIs not exposed by this wrapper.
requirements: The returned reference is only valid while the underlying QNetworkReply exists; do not store it beyond the callback/lifetime of the wrapper.
Do not delete or take ownership of the returned QNetworkReply; its lifetime is managed by Qt and the manager.

functions.name: utils::network::details::NetworkReply::retry
functions.description: Heuristic indicating whether the request may be retried. Returns true only for TemporaryNetworkFailureError or NetworkSessionFailedError.
requirements: Underlying QNetworkReply must still be valid when calling.
Caller decides policy on whether and how to retry; this function only checks specific error codes.

functions.name: utils::network::progress::received
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes received so far for a transfer progress event.
requirements: Meaningful within progress callbacks supplied to manager::get().

functions.name: utils::network::progress::total
functions.description: Returns the total number of bytes expected for the transfer, or 0 if unknown.
requirements: Meaningful within progress callbacks supplied to manager::get().

functions.name: utils::network::manager::QtNAM
functions.description: Provides access to the internal QNetworkAccessManager used by this manager. Useful to customize settings (e.g., proxies, cookies) before issuing requests.
requirements: The returned reference is owned by utils::network::manager; do not delete it.
Only use from the thread that owns the QNetworkAccessManager, typically the thread where the manager was created.

functions.name: utils::network::manager::get
functions.signature:
template<typename Reply, typename std::enable_if< std::is_void< utils::network::details::result_of<Reply, utils::network::reply> >::value, int >::type = 0>
void utils::network::manager::get(const QNetworkRequest& r, Reply reply) const
functions.description: Sends an HTTP GET and invokes the provided callback once with a utils::network::reply object when the operation finishes or times out.
requirements: Reply must be a callable invocable as void(const utils::network::reply&).
A running Qt event loop is required for signals/slots and the timer to operate.
The QNetworkRequest must be properly initialized (e.g., URL set).

functions.name: utils::network::manager::post
functions.signature:
template<typename Reply, typename Data>
void utils::network::manager::post(const QNetworkRequest& r, const Data& e, Reply reply) const
functions.description: Sends an HTTP POST with the given entity and invokes the callback once with a utils::network::reply object upon completion/timeout.
requirements: Reply must be a callable invocable as void(const utils::network::reply&).
Data must be a type accepted by QNetworkAccessManager::post (e.g., QByteArray, QIODevice*, or QHttpMultiPart*).
A running Qt event loop is required for signals/slots and the timer to operate.
The QNetworkRequest must be properly initialized (e.g., URL and headers as needed).

functions.name: utils::network::manager::head
functions.signature:
template<typename Reply>
void utils::network::manager::head(const QNetworkRequest& r, Reply reply) const
functions.description: Sends an HTTP HEAD request and invokes the callback once with a utils::network::reply object upon completion/timeout.
requirements: Reply must be a callable invocable as void(const utils::network::reply&).
A running Qt event loop is required for signals/slots and the timer to operate.
The QNetworkRequest must be properly initialized (e.g., URL set).

functions.name: utils::app::runMultiInstances
functions.description: Convenience entry point to run the application type specified by AppInfo without single-instance enforcement. Internally constructs utils::app::multipleInstance<AppInfo> with the provided info and starts the Qt event loop via QApplication::exec(). Intended when multiple concurrent instances are allowed.
requirements: AppInfo must define a nested type appType that is constructible from the type of AppInfo::args.
AppInfo must contain: args (constructor arguments for appType), socketPath (QString, not used here), app (QApplication&), and data (QByteArray).
appType must provide a method void start(QByteArray) which is invoked to start the application logic.
A valid QApplication instance must be referenced by info.app and its lifetime must outlive the call.
info.app.exec() will block until the Qt event loop exits.

functions.name: utils::app::make_oneinstance_args
functions.signature:
template <typename OIR, typename PIC>
auto utils::app::make_oneinstance_args(OIR r, PIC c) -> utils::app::instanceArgs<OIR, PIC>
functions.description: Factory helper that bundles two callbacks into an instanceArgs<OIR,PIC> value used by oneinstance/runOneInstance for single-instance coordination. The callbacks are invoked when another instance is detected or when a previous instance crashed.
requirements: OIR must be callable with signature void() and will be used as the handler for 'otherInstanceRunning'.
PIC must be callable with signature void() and will be used as the handler for 'otherInstanceCrashed'.
The returned object should be passed as the second argument to runOneInstance(AppInfo, Err) where Err has members otherInstanceRunning and otherInstanceCrashed.

functions.name: utils::app::runOneInstance
functions.signature:
template <typename AppInfo, typename Err>
int utils::app::runOneInstance(AppInfo info, Err err)
functions.description: Runs the application enforcing a single running instance using a local server/socket and a lock file. Uses the provided error/notification handlers in err for handling cases where another instance is already running or a previous instance crashed. Internally constructs utils::app::oneinstance<AppInfo, Err> and starts the Qt event loop.
requirements: AppInfo must define a nested type appType that is constructible from the type of AppInfo::args.

AppInfo must contain: args (constructor arguments for appType), socketPath (QString path used for QLocalServer/QLocalSocket and QLockFile with .lock suffix), app (QApplication&), and data (QByteArray).
appType must provide methods: void start(QByteArray) and void hasEvent(QByteArray).
Err must be a type that exposes two callable members: otherInstanceRunning() and otherInstanceCrashed().
A valid QApplication instance must be referenced by info.app and its lifetime must outlive the call.
socketPath should be a filesystem-safe name for QLocalServer::listen and QFile operations; if an existing stale socket file is detected, it may be removed.
info.app.exec() will block until the Qt event loop exits.

functions.name: utils::app::runOneInstance
functions.description: Overload that enforces a single running instance using default console handlers. If another instance is running, prints a message and exits; if a previous instance crashed, prints a message and attempts cleanup before starting. Internally builds default handlers via make_oneinstance_args and forwards to runOneInstance(AppInfo, Err).
requirements: Same requirements on AppInfo as the two-argument overload: appType constructibility, presence of args, socketPath, app, and data.
appType must provide: void start(QByteArray) and void hasEvent(QByteArray).
A valid QApplication instance must be referenced by info.app; info.app.exec() will block.

functions.name: utils::app::details::exec::exec
functions.description: Constructor for an internal helper QObject that schedules a callable to run on the Qt event loop using a queued connection. Upon construction, it connects its run signal to a private slot and immediately emits the signal, invoking the provided callable asynchronously.
requirements: Function must be invocable with signature void() and copyable/movable into std::function<void()>.
A running Qt event loop or an active QObject thread affinity is expected for queued delivery; otherwise the callable may run when the event loop starts.
The created object must live at least until the queued slot executes (managed here by member lifetime within owning objects).

functions.name: utils::app::details::exec::run
functions.description: Qt signal emitted by utils::app::details::exec during construction to trigger execution of the stored callable via a queued connection. Not intended for direct caller use; typically emitted internally.
requirements: This is a Qt signal; it is not a free-standing callable API for users. Emitting signals requires object context; external code should not rely on calling this directly.

functions.name: utils::app::AppTypeInterface::AppTypeInterface
functions.description: Minimal interface/base-pattern for application types consumed by the helpers. Accepts a struct containing a QApplication reference. Provided as documentation of the expected constructor shape of AppInfo::appType.
requirements: Caller must provide an args struct containing a valid QApplication&.
This type is illustrative; concrete appType implementations must be constructible from the same args type used in AppInfo.

functions.name: utils::app::AppTypeInterface::hasEvent
functions.description: Placeholder handler invoked in a single-instance scenario when a second instance sends data to the running instance. Real appType classes should implement an equivalent method to consume inter-instance messages.
requirements: QByteArray contains the data sent from another instance; semantics are application-defined.
No return value; should not throw exceptions across Qt signal/slot boundaries.

functions.name: utils::app::AppTypeInterface::start
functions.description: Placeholder startup entry point invoked when the first/only instance starts. Receives optional startup data (possibly forwarded from command-line or other sources). Real appType classes should implement an equivalent method.
requirements: QByteArray may be empty; semantics are application-defined.
Should initialize application state/UI and return quickly if used in event-driven contexts.

functions.name: utils::app::multipleInstance::multipleInstance
functions.description: Constructor for the multiple-instance runner. Stores AppInfo and schedules run() on the Qt event loop using the internal exec helper.
requirements: AppInfo must define a nested type appType and provide members: args, socketPath, app, data as described in utils::app::appInfo.
appType must be constructible from the type of info.args and have a method void start(QByteArray).
info is moved into internal storage; passed arguments should remain valid only through move.

functions.name: utils::app::multipleInstance::run
functions.description: Creates the main application object of type AppInfo::appType using stored constructor arguments and calls start(data). Intended to be invoked asynchronously by the internal exec helper; not a public API.
requirements: appType must have a constructor compatible with AppInfo::args and a method void start(QByteArray).
This method assumes the Qt event loop context; it is called after construction via a queued connection.

functions.name: utils::app::multipleInstance::exec
functions.description: Runs the Qt event loop by delegating to the QApplication stored in AppInfo. This should be called after constructing multipleInstance to start processing events.
requirements: AppInfo::app must reference a valid QApplication instance.
Blocks until the application exits and returns the exit code.

functions.name: utils::app::oneinstance::oneinstance
functions.signature:
template <typename AppInfo, typename InstanceArgs>
utils::app::oneinstance<AppInfo, InstanceArgs>::oneinstance(AppInfo info, InstanceArgs iargs)
functions.description: Constructor for the single-instance runner. Attempts to lock a .lock file, then schedules run() which coordinates with an existing instance (via QLocalSocket) or starts a new one (via QLocalServer). Uses iargs callbacks when another instance is detected or when a stale/crashed instance is cleaned up.
requirements: AppInfo must provide: args, socketPath (QString used for both QLocalServer socket name/file and .lock file), app (QApplication&), and data (QByteArray).
AppInfo::appType must be constructible from AppInfo::args and implement: void start(QByteArray) and void hasEvent(QByteArray).
InstanceArgs must expose callable members: otherInstanceRunning() and otherInstanceCrashed().
The process must have permissions to create/remove the socket file at socketPath and the lock file at socketPath + ".lock".
Qt event loop context required for signal/slot delivery; the constructor queues execution via an internal helper.

functions.name: utils::app::oneinstance::~oneinstance
functions.signature:
template <typename AppInfo, typename InstanceArgs>
utils::app::oneinstance<AppInfo, InstanceArgs>::~oneinstance()
functions.description: Destructor that, if this instance created and is listening on the local server, closes it and removes the socket file at socketPath. Ensures cleanup of IPC resources.
requirements: Socket file removal requires filesystem permissions.
Should be destroyed after the event loop has stopped accepting new connections to avoid races.

functions.name: utils::app::oneinstance::exec
functions.signature:
template <typename AppInfo, typename InstanceArgs>
int utils::app::oneinstance<AppInfo, InstanceArgs>::exec()
functions.description: Runs the Qt event loop by delegating to the QApplication stored in AppInfo. Used to start processing after coordinating single-instance behavior.
requirements: AppInfo::app must reference a valid QApplication instance.
Blocks until the application exits and returns the exit code.

import random
import struct

# This generator emits a length-prefixed sequence of byte strings to satisfy
# multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumptions. Each string is UTF-8 friendly for
# QString::fromUtf8 but may include embedded NULs and diverse Unicode.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

UNICODE_GROUPS = [
    (0x20, 0x7E),   # printable ASCII
    (0x09, 0x0D),   # tab, LF, VT, FF, CR
    (0x00A0, 0x00FF),  # Latin-1 supplement
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),  # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),  # Cyrillic
    (0x0600, 0x06FF),  # Arabic
    (0x0900, 0x097F),  # Devanagari
    (0x4E00, 0x4E5F),  # small CJK slice
    (0x2600, 0x27BF),  # Misc symbols incl. some emoji
]

EDGE_SUBSTRINGS = [
    b"",                              # empty
    b"\x00",                          # embedded NUL
    "\u00A0".encode("utf-8"),        # non-breaking space
    "\u200B".encode("utf-8"),        # zero-width space
    "\u2028".encode("utf-8"),        # line sep
    "\u2029".encode("utf-8"),        # paragraph sep
    "\uFFFD".encode("utf-8"),        # replacement char
    "\U0001F600".encode("utf-8"),    # 😀 (U+1F600)
]

PREFIXES = [b"", b"/", b"./", b"../", b"http://", b"https://", b"data:", b"file://"]
SUFFIXES = [b"", b"/", b"?q=", b"#frag", b".txt", b".bin", b"%00", b"%C3%A9", b"\n"]


def rng_codepoint(rnd):
    grp = rnd.choice(UNICODE_GROUPS)
    cp = rnd.randint(grp[0], grp[1])
    # Avoid surrogates to keep valid UTF-8
    if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
        cp = 0xFFFD
    return cp


def random_utf8(rnd, length):
    # Build a UTF-8 byte string of approximately 'length' characters.
    # We keep it valid UTF-8 by constructing from scalar values only.
    cps = [rng_codepoint(rnd) for _ in range(max(0, length))]
    s = "".join(chr(c) for c in cps)
    return s.encode("utf-8")


def random_mixed_bytes(rnd, length):
    # Mix ASCII control/printables with random UTF-8 sequences.
    out = bytearray()
    remaining = length
    while remaining > 0:
        style = rnd.choices(["ascii", "utf8", "nul"], weights=[3, 3, 1])[0]
        chunk = rnd.randint(1, min(16, remaining))
        if style == "ascii":
            for _ in range(chunk):
                out.append(rnd.choice(list(range(0x20, 0x7F)) + [0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D]))
        elif style == "nul":
            out += b"\x00" * chunk
        else:  # utf8
            out += random_utf8(rnd, chunk)
        remaining -= chunk
    return bytes(out)


def make_string_pair(rnd):
    # v: container string, opt: candidate prefix/substring/absent
    base_len = rnd.randint(0, 256)
    v_core = random_mixed_bytes(rnd, base_len)

    # Insert edge substrings at random positions
    for es in rnd.sample(EDGE_SUBSTRINGS, rnd.randint(0, min(4, len(EDGE_SUBSTRINGS)))):
        pos = rnd.randint(0, len(v_core))
        v_core = v_core[:pos] + es + v_core[pos:]

    # Optional URL-like wrapping
    if rnd.random() < 0.4:
        pre = rnd.choice(PREFIXES)
        suf = rnd.choice(SUFFIXES)
        middle = random_mixed_bytes(rnd, rnd.randint(0, 48))
        v_core = pre + middle + suf + v_core

    if len(v_core) > 1500:
        v_core = v_core[:1500]
    v = v_core

    r = rnd.random()
    if r < 0.20:
        opt = v
    elif r < 0.40:
        take = rnd.randint(0, len(v))
        opt = v[:take]
    elif r < 0.60:
        take = rnd.randint(0, len(v))
        opt = v[len(v) - take:]
    elif r < 0.80:
        if len(v) == 0:
            opt = b""
        else:
            a = rnd.randint(0, len(v))
            b = rnd.randint(a, len(v))
            opt = v[a:b]
            if rnd.random() < 0.3:
                opt = rnd.choice(EDGE_SUBSTRINGS) + opt + rnd.choice(EDGE_SUBSTRINGS)
    else:
        opt = random_mixed_bytes(rnd, rnd.randint(1, min(64, max(1, 256 - len(v)))))
        if opt in v and len(opt) > 0:
            opt = bytes([(opt[0] ^ 0xFF)]) + opt[1:]

    return v, opt


def ascii_fold(data, to_upper):
    out = bytearray()
    for b in data:
        if 0x61 <= b <= 0x7A and to_upper:
            out.append(b - 0x20)
        elif 0x41 <= b <= 0x5A and not to_upper:
            out.append(b + 0x20)
        else:
            out.append(b)
    return bytes(out)


def pack_len_prefixed(parts):
    out = bytearray()
    for p in parts:
        out += struct.pack("<I", len(p))
        out += p
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    v, opt = make_string_pair(rnd)

    parts = [v, opt]

    # Add some variants to widen coverage of contains/startsWith
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(ascii_fold(v, True))
        parts.append(ascii_fold(opt, True))
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(ascii_fold(v, False))
        parts.append(ascii_fold(opt, False))

    # Include a data: URL variant suitable for network-related stubs
    data_url = b"data:text/plain," + opt
    parts.append(data_url[:256])

    blob = pack_len_prefixed(parts)
    return blob[:MAX_TOTAL]

import os
import random
import struct
import sys

# Generator for buffers consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR / filename when fuzzing utils::qprocess::run
# Target expects interesting program paths and small argument payloads suitable for echo/printf.
# We craft a corpus entry that encodes:
# - A candidate executable path (from a curated list plus OS-appropriate variants)
# - Up to 3 short arguments, with bias towards printable UTF-8 and printf-like formats
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes
#
# Encoding format (simple length-prefixed frames):
#   [u8: program_index_hint]
#   [u8: argc (0..3)]
#   For each arg i in argc:
#       [u8: arg_kind]
#       [u16: length]
#       [bytes: payload]
#   [u8: extras_count (0..3)]  # additional small args consumed by extra FUZZ_PARAM_STR sites
#   For each extra j:
#       [u16: length]
#       [bytes: payload]
#
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR will draw from the single buffer; this payload provides a rich set of strings.

PRINTABLE = (
    [ord(c) for c in ("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_.:/\\ ")] +
    [9, 10]  # tab, newline
)

CANDIDATES = [
    b"/bin/true",
    b"/usr/bin/true",
    b"/bin/echo",
    b"/usr/bin/echo",
    b"/bin/printf",
    b"/usr/bin/printf",
    b"cmd.exe",
]

# Some interesting argument patterns
ECHO_PAYLOADS = [
    b"hello world",
    b"",
    b"unicode: \xce\xbb\xce\xb1\xce\xbc\xce\xb2\xce\xb4\xce\xb1",  # greek bytes
    b"spaces   and\ttabs",
    b"line1\nline2",
]

PRINTF_PAYLOADS = [
    b"%s",
    b"%d",
    b"%x %X",
    b"%p %n",  # interesting but harmless as string
    b"%-20s end",
    b"literal percent %% done",
]

EXTRA_SMALLS = [
    b"-n",
    b"-e",
    b"--help",
    b"%08x",
    b"A" * 16,
    b"\x00".replace(b"\x00", b""),  # effectively empty
]


def _rand_bytes_printable(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_utf8ish(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of printable ASCII and some UTF-8 sequences
    parts = []
    target = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.75:
            parts.append(_rand_bytes_printable(rng, 1))
        elif choice < 0.90:
            # 2-byte UTF-8
            ch = rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x07FF)
            parts.append(chr(ch).encode('utf-8'))
        else:
            # 3-byte UTF-8
            ch = rng.randint(0x0800, 0xFFFF)
            # avoid surrogates
            if 0xD800 <= ch <= 0xDFFF:
                ch = 0x2603
            parts.append(chr(ch).encode('utf-8'))
    data = b"".join(parts)
    return data[:max_len]


def _pick_program(rng: random.Random) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    # Weight OS-appropriate candidates
    cand = list(CANDIDATES)
    if os.name == 'nt':
        weights = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 5]
    else:
        weights = [3, 3, 5, 5, 4, 4, 1]
    idx = rng.choices(range(len(cand)), weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    return idx, cand[idx]


def _make_arg_for_program(prog: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    low = prog.lower()
    if b"echo" in low:
        base = rng.choice(ECHO_PAYLOADS + [
            _rand_utf8ish(rng, rng.randint(0, 48))
        ])
        return base
    if b"printf" in low:
        base = rng.choice(PRINTF_PAYLOADS + [
            _rand_utf8ish(rng, rng.randint(0, 48))
        ])
        return base
    if low.endswith(b"cmd.exe"):
        return b"/c"
    # default small token
    return _rand_utf8ish(rng, rng.randint(0, 32))


def _pack_u8(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('B', x & 0xFF)


def _pack_u16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('>H', x & 0xFFFF)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(int(seed))

    buf = bytearray()

    # Program
    prog_idx, prog = _pick_program(rng)
    buf += _pack_u8(prog_idx)

    # Argument count 0..3
    argc = rng.randint(0, 3)
    # Bias: if echo/printf, ensure at least 1 argument
    if b"echo" in prog.lower() or b"printf" in prog.lower():
        argc = max(1, argc)
    buf += _pack_u8(argc)

    for i in range(argc):
        # arg_kind: 0=random utf8, 1=echoish, 2=printfish, 3=flag, 4=newline
        if b"echo" in prog.lower():
            kind = rng.choices([1, 0, 3, 4], weights=[5, 2, 1, 1], k=1)[0]
        elif b"printf" in prog.lower():
            kind = rng.choices([2, 0, 3, 4], weights=[5, 2, 1, 1], k=1)[0]
        else:
            kind = rng.choices([0, 3, 1, 2, 4], weights=[5, 2, 1, 1, 1], k=1)[0]

        if kind == 0:
            payload = _rand_utf8ish(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
        elif kind == 1:
            payload = rng.choice(ECHO_PAYLOADS)
        elif kind == 2:
            payload = rng.choice(PRINTF_PAYLOADS)
        elif kind == 3:
            payload = rng.choice(EXTRA_SMALLS)
        else:
            payload = b"\n"

        # Special case for Windows cmd.exe: ensure fast exit by appending exit 0 when appropriate
        if prog.lower().endswith(b"cmd.exe") and i == 0 and payload == b"/c":
            # We will let the harness add extra args; ensure we also include an extra small set
            pass

        buf += _pack_u8(kind)
        buf += _pack_u16(len(payload))
        buf += payload

    # Extras used by additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR sites
    extras = rng.randint(0, 3)
    # Bias to add a newline for printf to terminate output quickly
    if b"printf" in prog.lower() and extras == 0:
        extras = 1
    buf += _pack_u8(extras)

    for j in range(extras):
        if b"printf" in prog.lower() and j == 0:
            pay = b"\n"
        else:
            pay = _rand_utf8ish(rng, rng.randint(0, 32))
        buf += _pack_u16(len(pay))
        buf += pay

    # Ensure buffer size cap
    return bytes(buf[:4096])

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: arbitrary binary data
# Used by fuzz stubs as QByteArray payloads transformed and sized.
# Goals:
# - Provide varied lengths, including 0, small, medium, near limits.
# - Include structured and high-entropy content to exercise different code paths
#   (e.g., size-based masks, reversals, XOR transformations).
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic given seed, but varied upon different seeds.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096

_ascii_words = [
    b"", b"a", b"test", b"payload", b"quick brown fox", b"lorem ipsum",
    b"\x00", b"\xff", b"\x00\x00\x00\x00", b"AAAAAA", b"BBBBBBBB",
]

# Prebuilt interesting binary patterns
_patterns: List[bytes] = [
    bytes(range(256)),                 # 0..255
    bytes(range(255, -1, -1)),        # 255..0
    b"\x00" * 64,
    b"\xff" * 64,
    b"\x55" * 128,
    b"\xaa" * 128,
    (b"ABCD" * 64),
    (b"\x00\xff" * 64),
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _mix_chunks(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    choices = _patterns + _ascii_words
    # Ensure at least one chunk
    while len(out) < target_len:
        kind = rng.randrange(6)
        if kind == 0:
            # pick from patterns
            chunk = rng.choice(choices)
            # maybe take a slice
            if chunk and rng.random() < 0.6:
                start = rng.randrange(0, len(chunk))
                end = rng.randrange(start, len(chunk))
                chunk = chunk[start:end]
        elif kind == 1:
            # random length ASCII
            l = min(target_len - len(out), rng.randint(1, 256))
            chunk = bytes(rng.choice(b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-_ ") for _ in range(l))
        elif kind == 2:
            # random binary block
            l = min(target_len - len(out), rng.randint(1, 512))
            chunk = _rand_bytes(rng, l)
        elif kind == 3:
            # run of a single byte
            b = rng.randrange(256)
            l = min(target_len - len(out), rng.randint(1, 1024))
            chunk = bytes([b]) * l
        elif kind == 4:
            # incremental counter bytes
            l = min(target_len - len(out), rng.randint(16, 256))
            start = rng.randrange(256)
            chunk = bytes((start + i) % 256 for i in range(l))
        else:
            # repeated short token
            token_len = rng.randint(1, 8)
            token = _rand_bytes(rng, token_len)
            reps = min((target_len - len(out)) // token_len, rng.randint(1, 64))
            if reps <= 0:
                reps = 1
            chunk = token * reps
        # avoid overshoot
        need = target_len - len(out)
        if len(chunk) > need:
            chunk = chunk[:need]
        out.extend(chunk)
    return bytes(out)


def _choose_length(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias toward interesting sizes used by the stubs (XOR mask uses size % 13)
    interesting = [0, 1, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129,
                   255, 256, 257, 511, 512, 1023, 1024, 2047, 2048, 4095]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(interesting)
    # otherwise random up to max
    return rng.randint(0, _MAX_SIZE)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    length = _choose_length(rng)

    # Sometimes return a single chosen canonical pattern exactly
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        base = rng.choice(_patterns + _ascii_words)
        if len(base) == length:
            return base
        # scale or trim to desired length
        if len(base) == 0:
            return b"" if length == 0 else bytes([0]) * length
        reps = (length + len(base) - 1) // len(base)
        return (base * reps)[:length]

    # Otherwise compose mixed content
    buf = _mix_chunks(rng, length)

    # Optional lightweight transformations to diversify but keep validity
    # - maybe reverse to align with qthread::run reversal path interplay
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        buf = buf[::-1]
    # - maybe XOR with a small mask similar to stub behavior
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and buf:
        mask = (len(buf) % 13) if (len(buf) % 13) != 0 else 7
        b = bytearray(buf)
        for i in range(len(b)):
            b[i] ^= mask
        buf = bytes(b)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(buf) > _MAX_SIZE:
        buf = buf[:_MAX_SIZE]

    return buf
